feature_results.rationale: Documented hooks (shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, prompts, subagents) fire on PreToolUse/PostToolUse and many other events, receive JSON context, and can return a decision. Mods additionally offer in-process handlers that can guard or change a tool call.

evidence.excerpt: Hooks are user-defined shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, LLM prompts, or subagents that execute automatically at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.
Your handler can then inspect the input, take action, and optionally return a decision.
Step into a tool call or a request: for example, hold a tool call while you ask the user a question, answer it without running the tool

constraints.description: Hooks fire in terminal, IDE extensions, Desktop app and cloud sessions; mod (in-process) hooks run in CLI, Desktop Code tab and VS Code extension.

feature_results.rationale: The local Bash sandbox routes network through a proxy with a configurable allowed/denied domain list (allowlist starts empty), and Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions have configurable network access (disabled or specific domains only). Enforceable via managed settings.

evidence.excerpt: No direct route out. Connections go through a proxy on your machine that checks each host against your allowed domains, which start empty.
`network.allowedDomains`, `network.deniedDomains`
Network access is limited by default and can be configured to be disabled or allow only specific domains

constraints.description: Local sandbox runs on macOS, Linux and WSL2; native Windows runs commands unsandboxed. Sandbox is off by default and covers shell commands only (WebFetch/WebSearch, MCP servers, hooks are outside it).
Cloud sessions are available on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise (premium/Chat+Claude Code seats).

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code automatically creates a checkpoint for each prompt and /rewind (or double Esc) can restore code and conversation to an earlier point in one operation. Caveat: only edits made via file editing tools are tracked; files changed solely by Bash commands and (usually) subagent edits are not restored.

evidence.excerpt: Every prompt you send that starts a turn creates a new checkpoint
Restore code and conversation: revert both code and conversation to that point
A file that only Bash commands changed isn't tracked and stays as it is.

constraints.description: Snapshots kept for the 100 most recent checkpoints per session and removed by retention sweep (~30 days by default, configurable via cleanupPeriodDays). Bash-only file changes and usually subagent edits are not restored; use Git.

feature_results.rationale: Admin-facing audit log export (180 days) exists for claude.ai organizations; Team/Enterprise analytics dashboard and spend report; OpenTelemetry export of metrics and events configurable by admins via managed settings; ZDR page lists audit logs among Enterprise admin capabilities; cloud sessions log all operations.

evidence.excerpt: all audit logs for the organization within the past 180 days will be aggregated.
Usage metrics: lines of code accepted, suggestion accept rate, daily active users and sessions
Track Claude Code usage, costs, and tool activity across your organization by exporting telemetry data through OpenTelemetry (OTel).
Audit logs
Audit logging: All operations in cloud sessions are logged for compliance and audit purposes

constraints.description: Analytics dashboard: Claude for Teams/Enterprise (claude.ai) and API Console; audit log export is an organization Owner function; the ZDR page lists audit logs as an Enterprise capability. The support article excerpt retrieved does not state plan tiers explicitly. Contribution metrics are beta and unavailable under ZDR.

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code documents dedicated review workflows: a managed Code Review service that reviews GitHub pull requests with inline comments, a local /code-review command for branch/PR diffs (with --fix and --comment), and a GitHub Actions review workflow.

evidence.excerpt: With Code Review, Claude reviews the pull requests in your GitHub repositories.
Findings arrive as inline comments on the lines concerned, ranked by severity, with a summary and a check run on the pull request.
`--comment`: posts the findings on a GitHub pull request as inline comments, or on a GitLab merge request as a single note

constraints.description: Managed Code Review service is available on Team and Enterprise plans only; local /code-review works on any plan.

Managed Code Review requires GitHub-hosted repositories (including GitHub Enterprise Server/Cloud with data residency) and the Claude GitHub App; not available with Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configuration or CMEK.

feature_results.rationale: Official common-workflows docs describe instruction-driven refactoring (e.g. 'refactor utils.js to use ES2024 features while maintaining the same behavior'), and the overview says Claude Code writes code across multiple files. Anthropic also links a large-scale code migration use case.

evidence.excerpt: refactor utils.js to use ES2024 features while maintaining the same behavior
For porting an entire codebase to a new language, see how Anthropic runs large-scale code migrations with Claude Code
Claude Code plans the approach, writes the code across multiple files, and verifies it works.

feature_results.rationale: Official common-workflows documentation has a 'Work with tests' recipe: identify untested code, generate test scaffolding on request, add edge-case tests, and run them, matching the project's existing frameworks. No framework/language restriction is stated.

evidence.excerpt: Claude can generate tests that follow your project's existing patterns and conventions.
add tests for the notification service

feature_results.rationale: Official docs describe an agentic loop in which Claude breaks work into steps, chains dozens of actions and verifies results autonomously, with the user able to interrupt. Permission prompts apply by default but can be reduced via permission modes/sandbox.

evidence.excerpt: Claude decides what each step requires based on what it learned from the previous step, chaining dozens of actions together and course-correcting along the way.
Claude works autonomously but stays responsive to your input.

constraints.description: Default permission model prompts for some actions; fewer prompts via permission modes or the sandbox.

feature_results.rationale: Ctrl+B backgrounds running Bash commands and agents, /tasks lists background shells and subagents, and web sessions let users kick off long-running tasks and check back later. Explicit completion-notification wording was not captured in the pages read.

evidence.excerpt: Backgrounds Bash commands and agents.
use [`/tasks`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands) to see running shells and subagents
Kick off long-running tasks and check back when they're done

constraints.description: Web/cloud sessions require a Claude subscription or Console account; terminal backgrounding via Ctrl+B.

access_gaps: Completion-notification behaviour not verified on a dedicated page

feature_results.rationale: Official docs describe file-pattern and regex content search plus language-server symbol navigation (via code intelligence plugins), but none of the fetched pages document a meaning-based/embedding index of the whole codebase. This is absence in the pages read, not a confirmed negative: pricing, changelog and product-page classes were not searched for indexing features.

queries: fetch how-claude-code-works (Search category: find files by pattern, search content with regex)
access_gaps: Changelog, product page and MCP/integration catalog not searched for semantic-index/embedding features; third-party MCP semantic search servers not assessed.

feature_results.rationale: Users can author custom subagents as markdown files with frontmatter (name, description, tools, model) and a system prompt in .claude/agents/ or ~/.claude/agents/, via --agents CLI flag, managed settings, or plugins.

evidence.excerpt: Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions.
You can also write subagent files by hand, define them via CLI flags, or distribute them through plugins.

access_gaps: Per-subagent MCP server attachment field not directly confirmed in fetched portion; optional criterion.

feature_results.rationale: The mods API lets a plugin register a tool for Claude with a name, description and JSON Schema input, handled by an in-process function (tool.call hook) rather than an external MCP server. Caveat: the tool is surfaced to Claude under an mcp__ prefixed name, though it is registered natively in-process.

evidence.excerpt: A tool is for Claude. Register it with a name, a description Claude reads, and a JSON Schema for its input.
You handle its calls in a tool.call hook filtered to that full name.

constraints.description: Mods work in the Claude Code CLI, Desktop Code tab and VS Code extension; behavior differs in claude -p and cloud sessions.
Mods are a newer plugin type; the registered tool is exposed to Claude with an mcp__<plugin>__<name> name.

feature_results.rationale: Anthropic publishes a DPA that is incorporated by reference into the Commercial Terms governing Team, Enterprise and API use (Claude Code under commercial terms).

evidence.excerpt: Data submitted through the Services will be processed in accordance with the Anthropic Data Processing Addendum ("DPA"), which is incorporated into these Terms by reference.
This Data Processing Addendum ("DPA") is incorporated into and forms part of the Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service or other agreement between Customer and Anthropic

constraints.description: Applies to commercial-terms customers (Team, Enterprise, API); consumer Free/Pro/Max plans are governed by Consumer Terms.

feature_results.rationale: Anthropic's first-party API offers inference_geo (global or US-only) and a Console workspace geo for at-rest storage, but the retrieved Claude Code docs do not document applying these to Claude Code itself, and only a US option was shown. Claude Code can also run via Amazon Bedrock/Google Cloud/Foundry where the customer picks the provider region, but I did not confirm region-specific Claude Code docs for that. Treated as partial pending confirmation.

evidence.excerpt: Inference geo: Controls where model inference runs, on a per-request basis. Set through the `inference_geo` API parameter or as a workspace default.
"us" | Inference runs only in US-based infrastructure.
Amazon Bedrock | AES-256 with AWS-managed keys. Customer-managed keys available via AWS KMS.

constraints.description: Documented geo options for the Anthropic API are global and US; no EU-specific option seen in retrieved text.
Region control applies to the API/workspace setup or third-party providers; applicability to Claude Code sessions on claude.ai plans is not documented in fetched pages.

access_gaps: No Claude Code-specific data residency page was fetched; Bedrock/Vertex region docs not checked.

feature_results.rationale: Consumer plans have a privacy setting to opt out of model training (opt-out yields 30-day vs 5-year retention); commercial plans are not trained on by default; Zero Data Retention available to qualified Enterprise accounts; local transcript retention adjustable via cleanupPeriodDays.

evidence.excerpt: We give you the choice to allow your data to be used to improve future Claude models.
Users who don't allow data use for model improvement: 30-day retention period
Anthropic does not train generative models using code or prompts sent to Claude Code under commercial terms
Zero Data Retention (ZDR) for Claude Code is available to qualified accounts on Claude for Enterprise.

constraints.description: ZDR is not part of the standard Enterprise plan; enabled per organization by the Anthropic account team after eligibility review. Training opt-out toggle applies to Free/Pro/Max; Team/Enterprise/API are excluded from training by default.
ZDR disables cloud sessions, feedback submission and some other features.

feature_results.rationale: Docs describe code-level vulnerability scanning (Claude Security plugin, /security-review, security-guidance) but explicitly place dependency scanners in the user's existing CI ('Your existing static analysis and dependency scanners'), implying no built-in CVE-database SCA. Not confirmed as not_found because changelog, product and MCP catalog classes were not checked.

access_gaps: Changelog, product page, MCP integration catalog not checked for SCA/CVE database integrations.

feature_results.rationale: In the VS Code extension's Manual permission mode, Claude shows a side-by-side comparison of original and proposed changes and asks permission, and the user can accept or reject before the file is written. The overview also states the JetBrains plugin has interactive diff viewing and the desktop app lets users review diffs visually. Per-hunk granularity was not confirmed on the pages read.

evidence.excerpt: In Manual mode, when Claude wants to edit a file, it shows a side-by-side comparison of the original and proposed changes, then asks for permission. You can accept, reject, or tell Claude what to do instead.
A plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, and other JetBrains IDEs with interactive diff viewing and selection context sharing.
Review diffs visually, run multiple sessions side by side, schedule recurring tasks, and start cloud sessions.

constraints.description: Diff review UI documented for VS Code extension (Manual permission mode), JetBrains plugin and Desktop app; in Auto/Edit-automatically modes edits are applied without asking.

access_gaps: VS Code page was truncated after the review-changes section; per-hunk accept/reject granularity not verified.

feature_results.rationale: Docs state TLS 1.2+ in transit and, per provider, AES-256 infrastructure-level disk encryption at rest for the Anthropic API (with provider-specific options for Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry).

evidence.excerpt: This data includes all user prompts and model outputs, encrypted in transit via TLS 1.2+.
Anthropic API | Infrastructure-level disk encryption (AES-256).

constraints.description: At-rest encryption depends on the model provider (Anthropic API, Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry).

feature_results.rationale: Claude for Teams includes SSO; Enterprise adds domain capture and role-based permissions; Console supports SSO and roles (Claude Code, Developer); managed settings can force login to a specific organization.

evidence.excerpt: Claude for Teams: self-service plan with collaboration features, admin tools, SSO, billing management, and server-managed settings for organization-wide Claude Code configuration.
Claude for Enterprise: adds domain capture, role-based permissions, and the compliance API.
Claude Code role: users can only create Claude Code API keys

constraints.description: SSO on Team and Enterprise; role-based permissions on Enterprise; Console roles for API customers.

feature_results.rationale: The first-party docs describe a product that signs in with a Claude account or API key and sends requests to a hosted model API, with proxy/CA and nonessential-traffic controls. None of the pages checked state that the product works with zero network connectivity or describe an air-gapped mode. Only documentation pages were checked, not every source class, so not_found cannot be asserted.

access_gaps: No web_search tool available; no targeted search for offline/air-gapped wording.
Pricing, changelog, and product page classes were not checked for this feature.
Fetched docs pages were truncated, so later sections were not read.

feature_results.rationale: Docs describe asking Claude to commit with a descriptive message, parallel sessions on separate git worktree branches via --worktree, and git-based workflows including commit and PR creation.

evidence.excerpt: Ask Claude to commit with a descriptive message and create a PR.
Each git worktree is a separate checkout on its own branch, created from an existing commit

feature_results.rationale: Non-interactive mode via claude -p with --allowedTools for pre-approval, --output-format json/stream-json, --json-schema structured output, documented exit codes (0 on success, non-zero on failure, 143 on SIGTERM), and --bare recommended for CI.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails, so your scripts can branch on the exit status.
`json`: structured JSON with result, session ID, and metadata
In CI or other scripted environments, add `--bare` so Claude Code starts without loading the host's hooks, plugins, auto memory, or `CLAUDE.md`.

constraints.description: Unattended runs require pre-approving tools (e.g. --allowedTools); --bare does not use subscription login and needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or a provider credential.

feature_results.rationale: None of the official pages read (overview, common workflows, VS Code) describe ghost-text or as-you-type inline completion; the product is documented as an agentic chat/CLI tool. Absence was not established through a complete protocol (no searches over pricing, changelog, product page, GitHub repo), so not_found is not justified.

access_gaps: No web search tool available (only web_fetch); product page, changelog, and GitHub repo not checked for inline completion.

feature_results.rationale: The Commercial Terms contain an IP indemnity for paid use and Outputs (Team, Enterprise, API). No public-code duplication filter setting was found in the fetched Claude Code docs, so only one of the two elements is documented. (Note: the has-criteria's 'or' wording could also support 'has'; partial chosen because partial-criteria explicitly covers only one of two.)

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic will defend Customer and its personnel, successors, and assigns from and against any Customer Claim

alleging that Customer’s paid use of the Services (which includes data Anthropic has used to train a model that is part of the Services) in accordance with these Terms or Outputs generated through such authorized use violates any third-party intellectual property right.

constraints.description: Applies under Commercial Terms (Team, Enterprise, API), not consumer plans; exclusions for modifications, combinations, customer inputs, etc.

access_gaps: Commercial terms fetch truncated after section M; no dedicated search for a public-code filter was run.

feature_results.rationale: CLAUDE.md instructions exist at managed-policy (organization), user (personal), project (repository) and local scopes, with a documented load order from broadest to most specific, applied automatically by concatenation (later/closer instructions read last). Note it is ordering in context, not hard override semantics.

evidence.excerpt: The table below lists them in load order, from broadest scope to most specific, so a project instruction appears in context after a user instruction.
All discovered files are concatenated into context rather than overriding each other.
Organization-wide instructions managed by IT/DevOps

constraints.description: Conflicting instructions are not hard-resolved: docs state Claude may pick one arbitrarily if two instructions contradict.

feature_results.rationale: Official docs describe routing Claude Code through customer-run gateways but explicitly state Anthropic does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway, and no documented Ollama/local-model backend was found in the pages checked. However, no web search tool was available, so the changelog, GitHub repo, and a full-text sweep of the docs were not exhausted; a not_found conclusion would not meet the auditable protocol.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic doesn't endorse, maintain, or audit third-party gateway products, and doesn't support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway.

access_gaps: No web_search tool available; changelog, GitHub repo, product page and rest of docs index not exhaustively checked for local/Ollama model support
llms.txt index was truncated after 20000 characters

feature_results.rationale: Dedicated documentation for monorepos/large codebases covers per-directory CLAUDE.md loaded on demand, path-scoped rules, claudeMdExcludes, read deny rules, LSP-based symbol lookup, subagents for exploration, and compaction with documented survival rules.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code works at any size, but as the codebase grows, the defaults tuned for smaller projects can fill the context window with instructions and file reads unrelated to the task
Code intelligence plugins connect Claude to a language server so it can jump to definitions, find references, and surface type errors directly instead of scanning the tree.
When a long session compacts, Claude Code summarizes the conversation history to fit the context window.

feature_results.rationale: Documented MCP support for connecting external tools and data sources, with a guide for building custom servers, plus a plugin system bundling skills, hooks, subagents and MCP servers.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code can connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open source standard for AI-tool integrations.
Plugins bundle skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers into a single installable unit from the community and Anthropic.

feature_results.rationale: The official Claude iOS/Android app has a Code tab that starts, monitors and steers Claude Code sessions (cloud sessions, Remote Control). Docs note there is no separate Claude Code mobile app and that code runs in the cloud or on the user's machine rather than on the phone.

evidence.excerpt: Start, monitor, and steer Claude Code tasks from your phone with the Claude app for iOS and Android.
Claude Code doesn't have a separate mobile app: cloud sessions and Remote Control both live in the **Code** tab in the Claude app

constraints.description: Requires a claude.ai account; not reachable with an Anthropic Console API key or third-party providers such as Amazon Bedrock. The Code tab may not be available on all plans.
Cloud sessions are aimed at GitHub repositories; the phone is a client, not where code runs.

feature_results.rationale: Documented subagents delegate side tasks in separate contexts, with built-in subagents (e.g. Explore) and automatic delegation; related docs cover background agents and coordinated agent teams.

evidence.excerpt: When Claude encounters a task that matches a subagent's description, it delegates to that subagent, which works independently and returns results.
For a coordinated team of sessions Claude spawns and supervises, see agent teams.

feature_results.rationale: The official overview states a single plain-language request leads Claude Code to write code across multiple files.

evidence.excerpt: Describe what you want in plain language. Claude Code plans the approach, writes the code across multiple files, and verifies it works.
It understands your entire codebase and can work across multiple files and tools to get things done.

feature_results.rationale: Official VS Code extension (also installable in Cursor) and a JetBrains plugin, in addition to a desktop app and terminal CLI. The JetBrains Marketplace listing is labelled beta, but VS Code is a distinct supported editor.

evidence.excerpt: The VS Code extension provides inline diffs, @-mentions, plan review, and conversation history directly in your editor.
A plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, and other JetBrains IDEs with interactive diff viewing and selection context sharing.

constraints.description: JetBrains plugin is listed on the marketplace as 'Claude Code [Beta]' and requires the CLI installed separately.

feature_results.rationale: Common workflows documents adding images (drag/drop, paste, path) and prompting e.g. 'Generate CSS to match this design mockup'.

evidence.excerpt: Generate CSS to match this design mockup
Drag and drop an image into the Claude Code window
What HTML structure would recreate this component?

feature_results.rationale: Overview documents describing features in plain language and getting code written, spanning multiple files, so granularity reaches multi-file.

evidence.excerpt: Describe what you want in plain language. Claude Code plans the approach, writes the code across multiple files, and verifies it works.
add tests for the notification service

constraints.description: Most surfaces require a Claude subscription or Anthropic Console account (or a supported third-party provider for CLI, VS Code, JetBrains).

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code offers customer-operated components: a self-hosted Claude apps gateway (built into the claude binary, deployed on Kubernetes/Cloud Run/own platform in the customer network) that routes inference to the customer's cloud provider account, and self-hosted environments (public beta) where cloud-session runners execute inside the customer network. The model inference itself is not run on-premises (outbound to Anthropic or a cloud provider), so this is not a full on-premises/private-cloud deployment of the service.

evidence.excerpt: Claude apps gateway is a self-hosted service that sits between your developers' Claude Code clients and your model provider.
A self-hosted environment executes Claude Code cloud sessions on infrastructure your organization operates.
Self-hosted environments are in public beta on Team and Enterprise plans and are off by default.
Organizations can deploy Claude Code through Anthropic directly or through a cloud provider.

constraints.description: Self-hosted environments are in public beta and off by default.
Self-hosted environments require Team or Enterprise plans.

Claude apps gateway requires an OIDC identity provider and an upstream provider (Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, or Anthropic API); inference is not run on-premises.
allowedProviders pinning of a custom endpoint requires Claude Code v2.1.285 or later.

feature_results.rationale: Docs document running parallel sessions with git worktrees, multiple sessions side by side in the desktop app, and multiple parallel tasks on the web.

evidence.excerpt: Run parallel sessions with worktrees so concurrent edits don't collide
run multiple sessions side by side
or run multiple tasks in parallel

constraints.description: Side-by-side sessions in the desktop app and parallel tasks on the web; worktree-based parallelism in CLI.

feature_results.rationale: Multiple permission modes (default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions) plus allow/ask/deny rules per tool layered on top, so file edits and shell commands can be configured independently.

evidence.excerpt: acceptEdits | Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands (mkdir, touch, mv, cp, etc.)
Modes set the baseline. Layer permission rules on top to pre-approve or block specific tools.

constraints.description: Auto mode requires a supported model and can be disabled by the organization.

feature_results.rationale: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md files, .claude/rules/, and auto memory persist guidance across sessions and load automatically at session start.

evidence.excerpt: Each Claude Code session begins with a fresh context window. Two mechanisms carry knowledge across sessions:
Auto memory: notes Claude writes itself based on your corrections and preferences

constraints.description: Instructions are treated as context, not enforced configuration; auto memory loads only the first 200 lines or 25KB.

feature_results.rationale: Plan mode explores read-only and blocks edits until the user approves a plan.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code blocks edits until you approve a plan

feature_results.rationale: Docs show asking Claude to 'create a pr' directly; Claude uses gh pr create or glab mr create (GitHub and GitLab CLIs) and links the session to the PR.

evidence.excerpt: You can create pull requests by asking Claude directly ("create a pr for my changes")
Claude Code links the session to the PR when Claude creates it with `gh pr create` or `glab mr create`

constraints.description: Relies on the gh (GitHub) or glab (GitLab) CLI being installed and authenticated; without gh it may fall back to the GitHub API with rate limits.

feature_results.rationale: A built-in OS-enforced Bash sandbox (off by default; enable with /sandbox) restricts filesystem and network access for shell commands; cloud sessions are isolated separately. Limits: shell commands only; not available on native Windows.

evidence.excerpt: The Bash sandbox is a boundary that the operating system enforces around the shell commands Claude runs on your machine.
The sandbox runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2. On native Windows, Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed.
The sandbox is off by default.

constraints.description: Local sandbox on macOS, Linux and WSL2 only; unsandboxed on native Windows.
Sandbox is off by default and covers shell commands only; file tools, MCP servers and hooks run outside it.

feature_results.rationale: Native scheduling exists: session-scoped /loop and cron tools, Desktop scheduled tasks, and cloud scheduled tasks (routines) that run without an open session or machine.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code offers three ways to schedule recurring or one-off work
For scheduling that survives independently of any session, create a [cloud scheduled task](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines.md), set up a [Desktop scheduled task]

constraints.description: /loop requires an open session (7-day expiry); Desktop tasks require the machine on; cloud tasks have 1-hour minimum interval.

feature_results.rationale: The only documented secret redaction found is narrow: when a user opts to share a session transcript after the feedback survey, known API key and token patterns are redacted before upload. No documented automatic secret detection/redaction of prompts sent to the model or of files written to disk was found in the pages checked (security, data-usage); users must rely on permissions, hooks, and sandboxing. Full-site coverage was not possible without search.

evidence.excerpt: Known API key and token patterns are redacted before upload. Source code, file contents, and other conversation content are uploaded as-is.

constraints.description: Redaction applies only to the optional session-transcript upload after the feedback survey, not to prompts sent to the model.

access_gaps: No web_search tool; settings reference, hooks docs and changelog not searched for secret-scrubbing options

feature_results.rationale: The documented agentic loop includes running tests, reading failures, editing and re-running tests to verify without a new prompt (verify phase repeats until task complete).

evidence.excerpt: Claude might: 1. Run the test suite to see what's failing
6. Run the tests again to verify
A bug fix cycles through all three phases repeatedly.

feature_results.rationale: Documented full-featured terminal CLI installed via native installer, Homebrew, WinGet, or Linux package managers, usable without any IDE.

evidence.excerpt: The full-featured CLI for working with Claude Code directly in your terminal. Edit files, run commands, and manage your entire project from the command line.

constraints.description: Requires a Claude subscription, Anthropic Console account, or a supported third-party provider.

feature_results.rationale: Code intelligence (LSP) plugins feed live diagnostics/type errors to Claude after its edits, and hooks (e.g. PostToolUse) can run linters/formatters automatically after edits.

evidence.excerpt: Claude catches type errors and missing imports that its own edits introduce before you run your build
Run shell commands automatically when Claude Code edits files, finishes tasks, or needs input. Format code, send notifications, validate commands, and enforce project rules.

constraints.description: Requires installing a language-server binary plus the matching code intelligence plugin per language.
Code intelligence plugins work in terminal sessions; cloud sessions do not start plugin language servers.

feature_results.rationale: Anthropic's DPA (incorporated into Commercial Terms) grants authorization for subprocessors listed in Schedule 4 and states the list is available at anthropic.com/subprocessors, which redirects to the Trust Center subprocessors page. The page is JavaScript-rendered so the itemized list contents could not be read via fetch; the existence of a published, publicly addressable list is established by the official DPA.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic's list of subprocessors is available at https://www.anthropic.com/subprocessors.
Customer grants Anthropic general authorization to engage the Subprocessors listed in Schedule 4, and any additional Subprocessors in accordance with Section C.3. below.

constraints.description: Disclosure is by Anthropic as the vendor of the underlying service, via the DPA for commercial customers.

access_gaps: Trust Center page is JavaScript-rendered; itemized list not readable via fetch

feature_results.rationale: Execution tools run shell commands, start servers, run tests and use git; commands are subject to the permission model (prompts, rules, or sandbox auto-approval).

evidence.excerpt: Execution | Run shell commands, start servers, run tests, use git
Claude Code can [run sandboxed commands without asking you](#sandbox-modes) to approve each one.

constraints.description: On native Windows, Bash tool needs Git for Windows, otherwise PowerShell is used.

feature_results.rationale: The official MCP docs list example third-party integrations (JIRA, GitHub, Sentry, Statsig, PostgreSQL, Figma, Slack, Gmail, Notion) and point to a vendor-run Anthropic Directory of reviewed connectors that can be added with `claude mcp add`. The vendor therefore documents and supports many third-party integrations and provides an official catalog.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code can connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources through the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Browse reviewed connectors in the Anthropic Directory. Directory connectors use the same MCP infrastructure as Claude Code, so you can add any remote server listed there with `claude mcp add`.

constraints.description: Integrations are delivered via MCP servers that the user must install/configure and trust; the docs warn to verify trust in each server.

access_gaps: The Anthropic Directory page (claude.ai/directory) and the MCP docs page remainder (truncated) were not fetched.

feature_results.rationale: The official overview documents a Web surface that runs Claude Code in the browser with no local setup, at claude.ai/code, covering core coding tasks on repositories.

evidence.excerpt: Run Claude Code in your browser with no local setup. Kick off long-running tasks and check back when they're done, work on repos you don't have locally, or run multiple tasks in parallel.
Start coding at claude.ai/code.

constraints.description: Most surfaces require a Claude subscription or Anthropic Console account.
Available on desktop browsers and the Claude app for iOS and Android.

additional_facts.description: Training and retention depend on the account type. Consumer users can choose whether their data is used to improve models (30-day retention when they decline), while code and prompts sent under commercial terms are not used to train generative models. Zero Data Retention is available only to qualified Claude for Enterprise accounts and disables some features such as cloud sessions.

evidence.excerpt: Users who don't allow data use for model improvement: 30-day retention period
Anthropic does not train generative models using code or prompts sent to Claude Code under commercial terms
Zero Data Retention (ZDR) for Claude Code is available to qualified accounts on Claude for Enterprise.

additional_facts.description: Claude Code connects to external tools and data sources through MCP, with a vendor-run directory of reviewed connectors that can be added with `claude mcp add`. A plugin system bundles skills, hooks, subagents and MCP servers into installable units.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code can connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources through the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Browse reviewed connectors in the Anthropic Directory. Directory connectors use the same MCP infrastructure as Claude Code, so you can add any remote server listed there with `claude mcp add`.
Plugins bundle skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers into a single installable unit from the community and Anthropic.

additional_facts.description: Subagents run in their own context windows with custom system prompts, tool access and permissions, and Claude delegates matching tasks to them automatically. The docs also describe agent teams: coordinated sessions that Claude spawns and supervises.

evidence.excerpt: Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions.
For a coordinated team of sessions Claude spawns and supervises, see agent teams.

use_cases.title: Long-running tasks delegated to the cloud
use_cases.description: Start long tasks in the browser or from the mobile app and check back later, or run several tasks in parallel.

evidence.excerpt: Kick off long-running tasks and check back when they're done
Start, monitor, and steer Claude Code tasks from your phone with the Claude app for iOS and Android.

use_cases.title: Creating and reviewing pull requests
use_cases.description: Ask Claude to commit changes and open a pull request, and have PRs reviewed either by the managed Code Review service on GitHub or locally with /code-review.

evidence.excerpt: You can create pull requests by asking Claude directly ("create a pr for my changes")
With Code Review, Claude reviews the pull requests in your GitHub repositories.

use_cases.title: Governed rollout in security-conscious organizations
use_cases.description: Inferred fit for organizations that need central control: SSO and role-based access, audit and telemetry export, a DPA and subprocessor list, a sandbox with network egress limits, and a self-hosted gateway or runners. It is not a vendor-stated use case and the on-premises story is only partial.
use_cases.rationale: Derived from the combination of already-verified governance, compliance and deployment features; no single official page presents this as a named use case.

use_cases.title: Non-interactive runs in scripts and CI
use_cases.description: Run Claude Code programmatically with `claude -p`, structured output and documented exit codes, with `--bare` recommended for CI.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails, so your scripts can branch on the exit status.
In CI or other scripted environments, add `--bare` so Claude Code starts without loading the host's hooks, plugins, auto memory, or `CLAUDE.md`.

use_cases.title: Writing tests and refactoring code
use_cases.description: Generate tests that follow the project's existing conventions and refactor code across files on instruction.

evidence.excerpt: Claude can generate tests that follow your project's existing patterns and conventions.
refactor utils.js to use ES2024 features while maintaining the same behavior

release_history.summary: Added CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL and an idle compaction setting; fork subagents are on by default in `claude -p`, the Agent SDK, desktop app and VS Code; 43 bug fixes.

evidence.excerpt: Changed fork subagents (`subagent_type: "fork"`) to be on by default in `claude -p`, the Agent SDK, the desktop app and VS Code, as they already are in the terminal
Bug fixes and reliability improvements

release_history.summary: Added Code Review levels (Quick, Standard, Deep), /auto-mode-setup, new mod hook capabilities, and tool search on by default behind custom gateways; 12 improvements and 43 bug fixes.

evidence.excerpt: Added review levels to Code Review: Owners choose Quick, Standard (the default), or Deep for the organization, and can give individual repositories their own level

release_history.summary: Added `sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces` for Linux sandboxed commands, improved /usage warnings with one-line fixes, and fixed a 2.1.304 regression that broke requests on Vertex, Bedrock and gateways rejecting tool search.

evidence.excerpt: Added `sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces` so sandboxed commands on Linux can create user namespaces (Chromium, rootless podman); this lets them get around the sandbox's file protections

release_history.summary: Fixed `claude -p` inside cloud sessions reporting not logged in, and an API error being replaced by a spurious prompt-too-long message in sessions with many MCP tools.

evidence.excerpt: Fixed `claude -p` inside cloud sessions reporting "Not logged in" when started without the session's environment variables

release_history.summary: Added the `claude_code.safety_event` OpenTelemetry event for tool calls stopped or prompted by permissions, auto mode, hooks or the sandbox; added `@claude review stop` to Code Review; 26 bug fixes.

evidence.excerpt: Added the `claude_code.safety_event` OpenTelemetry event for each tool call a permission rule, auto mode, a safety check, a hook or the sandbox stopped, prompted or sent back
Bug fixes and reliability improvements

release_history.summary: `sed -i` now follows the standard Bash prompt and is no longer restored by /rewind; `claude ultrareview` requires workspace trust; several sandbox fixes and 62 bug fixes.

evidence.excerpt: Changed `sed -i` to get the standard Bash prompt and run as written, not a simulated file-edit preview; like other Bash edits, it is no longer restored by `/rewind`

release_history.summary: Added the Monitor tool and plugin monitors on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry; added cloud sessions and Remote Control permissions to Enterprise custom roles; improved Linux sandbox diagnostics for AppArmor user-namespace restrictions; many bug fixes.

evidence.excerpt: Added Claude Code cloud sessions and Remote Control permissions to Enterprise custom roles, so Owners can control access to each by role
